conventions.latitudes: Horizons gives planetodetic latitudes on the reference ellipsoid of the header (radii_km: equatorial, polar); tan(graphic) = tan(centric) / (1 - f)^2 converts them.
conventions.longitudes: IAU 2015 prime meridians (System III for Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus), west-positive for Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn and Neptune, east-positive for Venus and Uranus. Horizons evaluates the rotation at the light time of the sub-observer surface point, (delta - R) / c, which a probe against Skyfield + DE440s confirmed (offsets of R / c of rotation otherwise).
conventions.np_ang: position angle of the north pole from the true-of-date celestial north, through east
conventions.time: TT; epochs outside 1990-2060 are for the deep-time tiers and are skipped by tests while the providers do not cover them

generator.description: JPL Horizons observer quantities for Mercury to Neptune, geocentric (CENTER 500@399), TT instants, quantities 2,9,10,11,13,14,15,17,19,20,24,32: apparent RA/Dec of date, APmag, illuminated percentage, defect of illumination, equatorial angular diameter, sub-observer and sub-solar planetodetic longitude and latitude, north-pole position angle and distance, r, delta, Sun-target-observer angle, and the pole's ICRF RA/Dec.
generator.licence: JPL Horizons (NASA/JPL-Caltech) states no terms for its output; used as a development-time reference only, never shipped (docs/THIRD_PARTY.md).
generator.never_a_runtime_dependency: Development-time reference. CONVENTIONS section 11: never regenerate a fixture from Rust output.
